text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zimbabwe press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Senior medical staff at Zimbabwe's two largest hospitals, Parirenyatwa and Harare, shut their doors to all patients on Wednesday as a two week strike by junior doctors and nurses which has crippled health services continued.

- Government officials have blamed state-owned Air Zimbabwe's long-standing operational problems on alleged interference in the running of the airliner's business activities and abuse of privileges by the company's board of directors and politicians.

- Zimbabwe's business sector is predicting an increase in United States investment and economic aid to the southern African country following U.S. president Bill Clinton's re-election for a second term of office on Tuesday.

- Zimbabwe's first syringe-making project in the eastern town of Marondera -- one of the largest industrial concerns owned by a black businessman -- is crumbling under the weight of big debts, lack of markets and raw materials.

- The Zimbabwean government has to meet some crucial conditions set by the European Union before the disbursement of Z$175 million for the southern African country's structural adjustment support programme.
- A local company with interests in the agricultural field, CFI Holdings, is seeking to list on the Zimbabwe Stock Exchange next year with a Z$50 million rights issue.

- One of the Zimbabwean capital Harare's oldest suburbs, Mbare, will receive a facelift under a Z$2 billion joint venture between the city council and a Malaysian construction company, Chase Perdana Berhad.
